newsitem.title: FRANCE: Romania must be in NATO first wave - Constantinescu.
newsitem.headline: Romania must be in NATO first wave - Constantinescu.

text.p: Romanian President Emil Constantinescu said in an interview published on Thursday it was essential his country be among the first wave of east European states admitted to NATO.

"From a military and strategic point of view, the expansion of NATO without Bucharest would have no meaning," Constantinescu told the newspaper Le Figaro ahead of a visit by French President Jacques Chirac to Romania starting Friday.
"It is essential that Romania be in the first wave of (east European) countries which join the Atlantic Allliance," he said.
Chirac is expected to be especially welcomed since he backs Bucharest's outsider bid to be among the first former Communist states admitted to the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation.

Chirac told Constantinescu in Paris this month that France "would plead strongly with its allies" for Romania to be among the first countries invited to join the 16-nation alliance at a summit in Madrid in July.

But U.S. officials accompanying Secretary of State Madeleine Albright on a European tour this week said Romania was still a "long shot" compared with favourites Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic.
Constantinescu vowed to icnrease Romania's military budget if admitted to NATO and pointed to a recent opinion poll showing 70 percent of Romanians backed that view.

Asked in a separate interview by the daily Le Parisien if a referendum might be called about Romania becoming a monarchy, he replied: "This is not a question one can put today. But it might be tomorrow."
Constantinescu's government recently restored Romanian nationality to exiled former King Michael who plans to return to Bucharest.
